slides.headline: How are you stretching?
slides.body: It is the first question I ask when someone tells me their stretching is not working. Six things I find myself saying in the clinic every single week.

slides.headline: Hard and short is the wrong recipe.
slides.body: Stretching is an instruction to the nervous system. Pull aggressively on a tight muscle and the nervous system tightens it further to protect itself.
slides.quoteText: Most people stretch too hard and too short.

slides.headline: Ramp into a stretch like you ramp into a lift.
slides.body: Two of ten. Then three. Then four. Treating a stretch like a one-rep max is how you tear something that thought it was relaxing.
slides.quoteText: You wouldn't max out on a squat right away — you'd warm up into it. Same with stretching.

slides.headline: Three of ten beats eight of ten.
slides.body: Start at an 8 and 8 is the ceiling. Start at a 3 and that 3 earns you a 4 next session, a 5 the session after. Range opens for the people who refuse to chase it.
slides.quoteText: If I start at 8, that's all I'm gonna get. If I start at 3, eventually I'll still be at 3 and I'll get further.

slides.headline: Your breath is the gauge.
slides.body: Holding your breath means the body is fighting the position. Slow even breathing means the body has permitted it. Breath tells you the truth before the muscle does.
slides.quoteText: If you're fighting yourself or holding your breath — it's too much.

slides.headline: Stretch is a feeling. Pain is information.
slides.body: A position that opens as a stretch and crosses into pain is telling you the entry was too aggressive. Back the dial down a notch and let the tissue come to you.
slides.quoteText: If it starts like a stretch and then builds into pain, you're starting too high.

slides.headline: Never push through dead pain.
slides.body: Sharp pain. Dull pain. Deep pain. All of it is a stop sign. Every millimeter of range is earned, never forced.
slides.quoteText: Never push through dead pain. Always progress systematically.

slides.body: If you have been stretching for years and the tightness keeps coming back, send me a DM and let's look at how you are doing it.
slides.tagline: Your threshold is higher than they told you.

caption:
How are you stretching?

It is the first question I ask whenever someone tells me their stretching is not working. Most people are pulling too hard, holding too short, breath locked, treating it like a one-rep max for the muscle.

Stretching is an instruction to the nervous system. Pull aggressively on something tight and the nervous system tightens it more. Slow, low, breath out, repeated. That is what opens range that stays.

If you start at an 8 out of 10, 8 is the ceiling. Start at a 3 and the 3 turns into a 5 over time. Most people skip that math and wonder why nothing changes.

If you have been stretching for years and the tightness keeps coming back, send me a DM and let's look at how you are doing it.

Be Good. Help Someone. Learn Lots.
